about: Date Flow step 3d: three long 'currents' for the Historical Currents layer (gap items 91-93), with their links.

spans.name: Axial Age
spans.description: The name the philosopher Karl Jaspers gave to the centuries when, in several regions at once, the Buddha, Confucius, the Hebrew prophets and the Greek philosophers set out ideas that shaped later religions and philosophies. Historians debate whether it was one shared turning point.
spans.note: Jaspers coined the term in 1949 and gave 800-200 BCE; others narrow or widen it. The concept itself is contested (some scholars call it a pattern imposed afterwards), so the description and significance say so, and its part_of links are medium confidence. Zoroaster is left out: his dates are too disputed.
spans.significance: The idea of an Axial Age points out that Buddhism, Confucianism, Greek philosophy and the teaching of the Hebrew prophets all took shape, largely independently, within a few centuries. Scholars still argue whether that reflects a real shared turning point or a pattern drawn afterwards.

spans.name: Age of Enlightenment
spans.description: An intellectual movement in Europe and its colonies that put reason, evidence and open debate at the centre of thinking about nature, religion and government. Writers such as Locke, Voltaire, Montesquieu, Rousseau and Kant argued over liberty, toleration and the limits of royal and church authority.
spans.note: No agreed start or end. 1685-1815 is a common broad framing (Newton's Principia 1687 and Locke's works around 1689 to the end of the Napoleonic Wars); French historians often use 1715-1789. Approximate for that reason.
spans.significance: Enlightenment ideas of natural rights, religious toleration, the separation of powers and government by consent shaped the American and French revolutions and much later liberal and democratic thought. Critics then and since have questioned its claims to universality and its uneven record on slavery and empire.

spans.name: Decolonization of Asia and Africa
spans.description: The decades after the Second World War in which most colonies in Asia and Africa became independent states, some through negotiation and others through long wars of independence. Membership of the United Nations nearly tripled.
spans.note: 1945-1975 is the main wave (to the independence of Portugal's African colonies); some accounts run on to Zimbabwe in 1980 or later. UN membership: 51 founding members in 1945, 144 by the end of 1975. Name keeps the scope honest: the Caribbean and Oceania also decolonized, mostly later.
spans.significance: Decolonization ended most European empires within a generation and remade the world map. It shaped the Cold War, as new states chose sides or stayed non-aligned, and left many borders, economies and conflicts that colonial rule had drawn.

links.why: The Buddha's teaching is one of the traditions Jaspers grouped into the Axial Age.
Confucius is one of the thinkers Jaspers placed at the heart of the Axial Age.
Greek philosophy, from Thales to Plato and Aristotle, is one of the Axial Age's main strands.
Explaining nature by reason and experiment inspired thinkers to apply the same methods to society and government.
Adam Smith was a leading figure of the Scottish Enlightenment.
Jefferson drew on Locke's ideas of natural rights and government by the consent of the governed.
Its articles on natural rights, popular sovereignty and the separation of powers echo Rousseau and Montesquieu.
The war drained the European powers and weakened colonial rule's prestige, strengthening independence movements.
Indonesia declared independence days after Japan's surrender, then fought the Dutch until 1949.
India's independence was the largest of the post-war transfers of colonial power.
Twenty-nine Asian and African states, many newly independent, met to oppose colonialism and Cold War pressure.
One of the bloodiest wars of independence, fought to end French rule in Algeria.
Ghana's independence under Kwame Nkrumah became a model for movements across Africa.
Seventeen African states, mostly former French colonies and trust territories, became independent in one year.
